results.title: Introduction to Human-Computer Interaction | Oxford Academic
results.content: Essential activities in this field concern understanding people, studying what users need and want, designing and engineering interactive systems, and evaluating their benefits to users. Ultimately, the purpose of HCI research is to influence the design of applications, interaction techniques, systems, or services so that users can achieve their goals in an effective, efficient, safe, and satisfactory manner. The skills cover software development, such as understanding software architectures and programming user interfaces; analytical skills, such as formal modeling of a user’s performance; design practice, for example, interaction design, service design, or product design; and user research skills, such as carrying out and analyzing experiments, conducting interviews, and engaging in field studies. Therefore, as computing spreads to broader user groups and new contexts of use, HCI is needed to make interactive systems usable and useful. results.title: Design and Quality for Biomedical Technologies XIX
results.content: We have developed a non-clinical bench test method using a mock cardiovascular flow loop and tissue-mimicking finger phantom that can simulate bio-realistic pulsation at controlled blood oxygen saturation (SaO2) levels. Design of a microfluidic blood flow phantom to address skin tone bias in multispectral imaging for nailfold capillaroscopy. Standardized tissue-mimicking phantoms for quantitative photoacoustic imaging (Invited Paper). SFDI is finding utility in a wide array of applications, including burn assessment, skin cancer detection, tumor monitoring, brain imaging, vascularization studies, and evaluating food quality—thanks to its non-invasive, wide-field, and depth-sensitive optical property mapping capabilities. Design of Lipid Emulsion-Dye Phantoms for Validation of Optical Imaging Systems. The homemade lipid emulsion-dye phantom has a low cost and tunability and can provide a more accessible approach to validating various optical imaging systems. Gelatin-based tissue-simulating skin phantom for the optimization of enhanced thermal imaging (ETI). The development of tissue-simulating phantoms to validate the quality and precision of medical imaging systems is a well-established field.

results.title: Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards: Child Restraint ...
results.content: This final rule amends FMVSS No. 213, “Child restraint systems,” [1]  and adds FMVSS No. 213b, “Child restraint systems; Mandatory applicability beginning December 5, 2026.” The amendments to FMVSS No. 213, mandatory in one year, modernize the standard by updating the CRS owner registration program, labeling requirements instructing consumers on correct use of child restraints, requirements for add-on school bus-specific child restraint systems, and provisions for NHTSA's use of test dummies in NHTSA compliance tests. 2. Under this final rule, NHTSA will test child restraint systems with internal components [3]  that restrain the child for compliance while the CRS is attached to the updated standard seat assembly with a Type 2 belt.[4]  However, in response to comments, the rule retains until September 1, 2029, the requirement that these CRSs must meet the standard's requirements when attached to the updated standard seat assembly with a Type 1 belt (S5.3.2).[5]  This provision will provide time for on-road vehicles to change over to a passenger vehicle fleet that will have Type 2 belts in nearly all rear seats.
